extracted.intended_audience: federal agency EEO/HR officials, agency counsel, administrative judges, and others responsible for handling federal EEO complaints and Rehabilitation Act Plans
extracted.subtask_short: EEOC complaint procedures and disability plans
extracted.subtask_description: Federal regulatory standards for processing individual EEO complaints (investigations, hearings, final agency actions, offers, discovery, summary judgment, records) and for agency Rehabilitation Act affirmative action/reasonable accommodation/accessibility and personal assistance service plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for failure to respond to documentary/witness requests (investigator/decisionmaker/Commission)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the complainant, or the agency against which a complaint is filed, or its employees fail without good cause shown to respond fully and in timely fashion to requests for documents, records, comparative data, statistics, affidavits, or the attendance of witness(es), the investigator may note in the investigative record that the decisionmaker should, or the Commission on appeal may, in appropriate circumstances:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (i) Draw an adverse inference that the requested information or testimony would have reflected unfavorably on the non‑producing party; (ii) Consider the matters to which the information/testimony pertains to be established in favor of the opposing party; (iii) Exclude other evidence offered by the non‑producing party; (iv) Issue a decision fully or partially in favor of the opposing party; or (v) Take such other actions as it deems appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigators and hearing officials must have appropriate security clearances
rubrics_metrics.description: Any investigation will be conducted by investigators with appropriate security clearances. Any hearing will be conducted by an administrative judge or hearing examiner with appropriate security clearances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission will, upon request, supply the agency with the name of an investigator with appropriate clearances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency investigation timeline and permissible extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall complete its investigation within 180 days of the date of filing of an individual complaint (or within time ordered on appeal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By written agreement the complainant and agency may voluntarily extend up to an additional 90 days. The agency may unilaterally extend up to 30 days to sanitize classified material (Exec. Order No. 12356 or successor), provided the agency notifies the parties of the extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of investigative file and notice of hearing/decision rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 180 days (or applicable amended timelines), the agency shall provide the complainant with a copy of the investigative file and shall notify the complainant that, within 30 days of receipt, the complainant has the right to request a hearing before an administrative judge or may request an immediate final decision from the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice must inform the complainant that the hearing request may be filed using the EEOC Public Portal (https://publicportal.eeoc.gov).

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency duty to notify complainant when investigation not completed on time
rubrics_metrics.description: If the agency does not send the notice required within the applicable time limits, it shall issue a written notice informing the complainant that it has been unable to complete the investigation within required time limits and estimate a completion date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice must explain that the complainant may request a hearing or file a civil action, and must contain information about hearing procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complainant's right and procedure to request a hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the complainant has received the notice or at any time after 180 days from filing, the complainant may request a hearing by submitting a written request to the EEOC office indicated or via the EEOC Public Portal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The complainant must send a copy of the request to the agency EEO office. Within 15 days of receipt, the agency shall provide a copy of the complaint file to EEOC and, if not previously provided, to the complainant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment and adjudicative responsibility of administrative judge
rubrics_metrics.description: When a complainant requests a hearing, the Commission shall appoint an administrative judge to conduct a hearing in accordance with §1614.109. Upon appointment, the administrative judge shall assume full responsibility for adjudication, including overseeing development of the record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any hearing will be conducted by an AJ or hearing examiner with appropriate security clearances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative judge authority to dismiss complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative judges may dismiss complaints pursuant to §1614.107, on their own initiative (after notice to parties), or upon an agency's motion to dismiss.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dismissal authority follows the standards and processes set out in §1614.107.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer of resolution — permissible timing
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may make an offer of resolution any time after filing the written complaint but not later than the date an administrative judge is appointed; and after appointment, but not later than 30 days prior to the hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offers before AJ appointment are limited to complainants represented by counsel; after appointment, offers may be made whether or not complainant has counsel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer of resolution — required content and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: The offer must be in writing and include notice explaining possible consequences of failing to accept the offer. To be effective the offer must include attorney's fees and costs and specify any non‑monetary relief; monetary relief may be lump sum or itemized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complainant has 30 days to accept in writing (postmarked or received within 30 days). If complainant fails to accept and the ultimately awarded relief is not more favorable than the offer, complainant generally shall not receive payment of attorney's fees or costs incurred after the 30‑day period, except where interest of justice requires otherwise. Agencies may make further offers and parties may negotiate at any time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery rights, scope, and authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: The administrative judge shall notify parties of the right to seek discovery and may issue discovery orders as appropriate. Unless parties agree in writing on methods and scope, the party seeking discovery must request authorization from the AJ prior to commencing discovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both parties entitled to reasonable development of evidence relevant to the issues. AJ may limit quantity and timing. Methods: interrogatories, depositions, requests for admissions, stipulations, production of documents. Valid objections include irrelevance, overburdensome, repetitious, or privilege.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct of hearings — witness attendance, closed hearings, and AJ powers
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall provide attendance for all employees approved as witnesses by the AJ. Attendance is limited to persons with direct knowledge relating to the complaint. Hearings are part of the investigative process and are closed to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The AJ may regulate conduct, limit number of witnesses (avoid repetitious testimony), exclude persons for contumacious conduct or misbehavior, receive evidence relevant to the complaint, and exclude irrelevant or repetitious evidence. The AJ or Commission may refer attorneys for disciplinary action or suspend/disqualify representatives for refusing to follow AJ orders or for improper conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural obligations to produce evidence and oath/penalty of perjury
rubrics_metrics.description: Complainant, agency, and any federal employee shall produce documentary and testimonial evidence as the AJ deems necessary. The AJ shall serve orders to produce evidence on both parties and is authorized to administer oaths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Witness statements shall be made under oath or affirmation or, alternatively, by written statement under penalty of perjury.

rubrics_metrics.name: AJ sanctions for failing to respond to AJ orders or requests
rubrics_metrics.description: When a party or its employees fail without good cause to respond fully and timely to an AJ order or requests for the investigative file, documents, records, statistics, affidavits, or witness attendance, the AJ shall, in appropriate circumstances, take sanctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sanctions include: (i) drawing adverse inference; (ii) considering matters established for opposing party; (iii) excluding other evidence; (iv) issuing decision fully/partially for opposing party; or (v) taking other appropriate actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary judgment procedure before hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: If a party believes material facts are not in genuine dispute, the party may file, at least 15 days prior to hearing (or earlier if ordered), a statement with the AJ setting forth the facts and record references demonstrating no genuine issue of material fact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statement must be served on the opposing party. Opposing party may file an opposition within 15 days or submit an affidavit explaining inability to present facts. After considering submissions the AJ may order discovery, limit the hearing to issues remaining, issue a decision without a hearing, or make other appropriate rulings.

rubrics_metrics.name: AJ-initiated summary disposition
rubrics_metrics.description: If the AJ determines on his/her own initiative that some or all facts are not in genuine dispute, the AJ may, after notice and providing parties opportunity to respond in writing within 15 calendar days, issue an order limiting scope of hearing or issue a decision without holding a hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AJ must provide notice and opportunity to respond before issuing such order or decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record and transcript obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: The hearing shall be recorded and the agency shall arrange and pay for verbatim transcripts. All documents submitted to and accepted by the AJ become part of the hearing record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the agency submits an accepted document, it shall furnish a copy to the complainant. If the complainant submits an accepted document, the AJ shall make it available to the agency representative for reproduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative judge decision timing and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless good cause for extension is written, an AJ shall issue a decision and order appropriate remedies/relief where discrimination is found within 180 days of receipt by the AJ of the complaint file from the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The AJ shall transmit copies of the hearing record, transcript, and decision to the parties. If the agency does not issue a final order within 40 days of receipt of the AJ's decision, the AJ's decision becomes the final agency action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency final action after AJ decision (40‑day requirement and required contents)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an AJ has issued a decision, the agency shall take final action by issuing a final order within 40 days of receipt of the hearing file and AJ decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final order must notify the complainant whether the agency will fully implement the AJ decision; contain notice of the right to appeal to EEOC and to file a civil action in federal district court, name the proper defendant, state applicable time limits for appeals and lawsuits; attach a copy of EEOC Form 573. If final order does not fully implement the AJ decision, the agency shall simultaneously file an appeal under §1614.403 and append a copy of the appeal to the final order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency final action in other circumstances (60‑day requirement and required contents)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an agency dismisses entire complaint, receives request for immediate final decision, or does not receive a reply to the notice under §1614.108(f), the agency shall take final action by issuing a final decision within 60 days of notification or of the end of the 30‑day period for complainant's choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final decision must consist of findings on the merits of each issue or rationale for dismissing claims and, when discrimination is found, appropriate remedies and relief in accordance with subpart E. The final action must contain notice of appeal and civil action rights and attach EEOC Form 573.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice that appeals may be filed via EEOC Public Portal
rubrics_metrics.description: When an agency's final order/decision must include a notice that the complainant has the right to appeal to the EEOC, the notice shall inform the complainant that the appeal may be filed using the EEOC Public Portal (https://publicportal.eeoc.gov).

rubrics_metrics.name: ADEA alternative civil action notice requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: As an alternative to filing an EEOC complaint under this part, an aggrieved individual may file a civil action in a U.S. district court under the ADEA after giving the Commission at least 30 days' notice of the intent to file such action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such notice must be filed in writing with EEOC (P.O. Box 77960, Washington, DC 20013) or by personal delivery or facsimile within 180 days of the occurrence of the alleged unlawful practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission authority to exempt positions from ADEA by BFOQ determination
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may exempt a position from ADEA provisions if it establishes a maximum age requirement for the position based on a determination that age is a bona fide occupational qualification necessary to the performance of the duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal Pay Act enforcement and processing
rubrics_metrics.description: In enforcing the Equal Pay Act (EPA), the Commission has authority to investigate an agency's employment practices on its own initiative to determine compliance, and will provide notice to the agency of such investigations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complaints alleging violations of the EPA shall be processed under this part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rehabilitation Act nondiscrimination standard (Section 501 equivalence to ADA standards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal agencies shall not discriminate on the basis of disability in hiring, advancement, discharge, compensation, training, or other terms/conditions/privileges of employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The standards used to determine whether Section 501 has been violated shall be the standards applied under the ADA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Government duty as a model employer and affirmative action requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal Government shall be a model employer of individuals with disabilities; agencies shall give full consideration to hiring, advancement, and retention of qualified individuals with disabilities and take affirmative action to promote recruitment, hiring, and advancement to eliminate under‑representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to adopt and implement an affirmative action Plan meeting specified criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 29 U.S.C. 791, each agency shall adopt and implement a Plan that provides sufficient assurances, procedures, and commitments to provide adequate hiring, placement, and advancement opportunities for individuals with disabilities at all levels of federal employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An agency fails to satisfy this requirement unless it has adopted and implemented a Plan that meets the enumerated criteria in the regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan: disability hiring and advancement program — recruitment obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Plan shall require the agency to take specific steps to ensure a broad range of individuals with disabilities, including targeted disabilities, will be aware of and encouraged to apply for vacancies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At minimum, include: (A) use of programs/resources that identify applicants with disabilities (e.g., training/internship programs, databases, programs leading to qualifications); and (B) establishment and maintenance of contacts (including formal agreements) with organizations that assist individuals with disabilities (American Job Centers, State Vocational Rehab, Centers for Independent Living, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan: application process — designated staff and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Plan shall ensure the agency has designated sufficient staff to handle disability‑related issues in application/selection processes and shall require training, support, and resources for them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responsibilities include: (A) ensuring disability‑related questions are answered promptly and correctly (including reasonable accommodations and hiring authorities); (B) processing requests for reasonable accommodations during application and placement and providing accommodations when required under part 1630; (C) accepting applications for appointment under hiring authorities that take disability into account; (D) determining eligibility for such hiring authorities and forwarding applications with explanations to hiring officials; (E) overseeing other agency programs designed to increase hiring of individuals with disabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan: advancement program to ensure promotion opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Plan shall require agencies to take steps to ensure current employees with disabilities have sufficient opportunities for advancement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include ensuring employees are informed of and have opportunities to enroll in relevant training (including management training), development/maintenance of mentoring programs, and administration of exit interviews that ask how to improve recruitment, hiring, inclusion, and advancement of individuals with disabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan: disability anti‑harassment policy requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Plan shall require the agency to state specifically in its anti‑harassment policy that harassment based on disability is prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Plan must include in its training materials examples of conduct that would constitute disability‑based harassment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan: general reasonable accommodation procedures requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Plan shall require the agency to adopt, post on its public Web site, and make available to all job applicants and employees in written and accessible formats reasonable accommodation procedures that are easy to understand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These procedures must include a wide range of required elements (see separate subcriteria) and govern how requests are made, processed, tracked, and decided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable accommodation procedures: define terms and explain reassignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures must explain relevant terms (e.g., 'reasonable accommodation,' 'disability,' 'interactive process,' 'qualified,' 'undue hardship') using examples, and explain that reassignment to a vacant qualified position is a reasonable accommodation and must be considered when no other accommodation will allow performance of essential functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable accommodation procedures: supervisor duties and vacancy searches
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures must notify supervisors and relevant employees how and where to conduct searches for available vacancies when considering reassignment as an accommodation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable accommodation procedures: how requests may be made
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures must explain that an individual may request reasonable accommodation orally or in writing at any time, need not fill out any specific form, and need not have a particular accommodation in mind; requests may be made to supervisors, the office designated to oversee accommodations, application process employees, or any designated agency employee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms used must be attached and available in alternative accessible formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable accommodation procedures: interactive process and decision contact
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures must describe the agency's process for determining whether to provide an accommodation, including the interactive process, and provide contact information for the individual or program office from whom requesters will receive a final decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require decision makers to communicate early in and periodically throughout the interactive process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable accommodation procedures: medical information rules and confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures must explain when the agency may require medical information sufficient to explain the disability, need for reasonable accommodation, and how the requested accommodation assists job performance; when agency may request supplemental medical info; and that agency may have medical information reviewed by a medical expert at agency expense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures must explain the agency's obligation to keep medical information confidential and the limited circumstances under which it may be disclosed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable accommodation procedures: timelines, interim accommodations, and expedited processing
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures must designate the maximum time (absent extenuating circumstances) the agency has to either provide or deny an accommodation and explain that the time begins when the accommodation is first requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures must state that usual timelines may not apply if a health professional delays documentation, that failure to provide an accommodation promptly (when it could have been provided sooner) may constitute a violation, provide for expedited processing for urgent needs, and require interim accommodations when entitlement is reasonably likely but full accommodation cannot be immediately provided, unless undue hardship would result.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable accommodation procedures: tracking, delay notices, dispute resolution, and complaint rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures must inform applicants/employees how to track processing of requests, require notification of reasons for delay (including extenuating circumstances), encourage voluntary informal dispute resolution, provide that individuals denied accommodations have the right to file complaints under 29 CFR 1614.106, and require a notice at time of denial consistent with specific content requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures must include information on how to access additional information (Commission guidance and technical assistance documents).

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan: steps to avoid denial of accommodations due to cost
rubrics_metrics.description: The Plan shall require the agency to take specific steps to ensure requests for reasonable accommodation are not denied for reasons of cost where agency resources (excluding certain statutorily designated funds) would enable provision without undue hardship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At minimum: (A) ensure decision makers know that all resources available to the agency as a whole (excluding designated funds) are considered when determining undue hardship under 29 CFR part 1630; and (B) ensure decision makers know how to arrange for use of agency resources, including any centralized fund for accommodations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan: notification requirements when accommodation is denied
rubrics_metrics.description: The Plan shall require the agency to provide a job applicant or employee who is denied a reasonable accommodation with a written notice at the time of denial, in an accessible format when requested, that explains the reasons for denial and notifies of available internal appeals or informal dispute resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice must inform the individual of the right to challenge the denial by filing a complaint under this part, provide instructions on how to file, and explain that the right to file a complaint will be lost unless contact with an EEO Counselor is initiated within 45 days of the denial (per 29 CFR 1614.105).

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan: accessibility of facilities and technology notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The Plan shall require the agency to adopt, post on its public Web site, and make available to all employees in written and accessible formats a notice explaining rights under Section 508 (accessibility of agency technology) and the Architectural Barriers Act (accessibility of buildings/facilities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice must provide contact information for employees responsible for physical accessibility and for electronic/information technology accessibility, and provide instructions on how to file complaints alleging violations of these accessibility requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan: assistance when another entity is responsible for accessibility violations
rubrics_metrics.description: If an agency's investigation of a complaint under Section 508 or the Architectural Barriers Act shows a different entity is responsible, the Plan shall require the agency to inform the individual where he or she may file a complaint against that other entity, if possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan: obligation to provide personal assistance services (PAS)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Plan shall require the agency to provide an employee with personal assistance services during work hours and job‑related travel in addition to professional services required as a reasonable accommodation when: (A) the employee requires such services because of a targeted disability; (B) provision of such services would, together with any required reasonable accommodations, enable the employee to perform essential job functions; and (C) provision would not impose undue hardship on the agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan: personal assistance services provider rules and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Plan shall state that PAS must be performed by a personal assistance service provider. The Plan may permit agencies to require PAS providers to serve more than one individual and may permit providers to perform tasks unrelated to PAS only to the extent that doing so does not result in failure to provide required PAS in a timely manner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan: prohibition on adverse actions for need for PAS
rubrics_metrics.description: The Plan shall prohibit the agency from taking adverse actions against job applicants or employees based on their need for, or perceived need for, personal assistance services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan: selection preference for personal assistance service providers
rubrics_metrics.description: When selecting someone to provide PAS to a single individual, the Plan shall require the agency to give primary consideration to the individual's preferences to the extent permitted by law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan: written procedures for processing PAS requests
rubrics_metrics.description: The Plan shall require the agency to adopt, post on its public Web site, and make available to all job applicants and employees in written and accessible formats procedures for processing requests for personal assistance services.
